verdict: The round-10 finding resolves as stated: 06 6.4, J1 step 5, 05 5.4 and B2 now agree that ssh-add -c needs a program SSH_ASKPASS can name, installed first, and B2 records the outcome with none. The delta adds one Required gap (the import-closure rule for pr against the YAML dependency pr needs) and one Advisory (stale command lines).

findings.defect: The rule says the import closure of tools/ci/pr is the standard library and paths on approvals, and a test fails on any other path in go list -deps. But pr reads .github/ask-first.yaml and docs/grants.yaml, and 12.1 lists go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 as the only YAML reader (there is no stdlib YAML). pr also needs git invocation (internal/gitsafe or its own) and canonical sha256 helpers. The spec does not say how pr parses YAML or which shared packages are placed on approvals.
findings.scenario: The task that builds pr (T005) imports go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 as 12.1 tells it to: the go list -deps test fails. The implementer either adds the module path to the globs (so a go.mod bump, now on dependencies and grantable, changes code that runs in the grant-judging job, defeating the point) or hand-writes a YAML parser, or reads internal/gitsafe, which is on no approvals glob and is not built until later.
findings.change: State in 05 5.3 which dependencies pr may import: either pr parses the two files in a format it owns (not YAML), or the third-party YAML module and its version in go.mod/go.sum are named as an accepted grantable input in the same Deferred row as the toolchain; and say whether internal/gitsafe is on approvals or pr carries its own hardened git calls. Make the go list -deps test's allowed set match.

findings.section: 12 12.4 (command block lines 164-165); plan T005; 10 10.2 pr row
findings.defect: The command block still shows go run ./tools/ci pr <payload file> and go run ./tools/ci pr --title ... , while the pr job grammar (10.2) allows only go run ./tools/ci/pr and 10.2/12.4 now run it that way. One sentence in 12.4 says the prose 'tools/ci pr' means the package, but a command line copied from the block would invoke a subcommand of tools/ci that no longer exists.

findings.change: Write go run ./tools/ci/pr in the 12.4 command block and in plan T005, keeping the explanatory sentence for prose.
